title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Dispersion — 2020
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Differentiate between deviation of light and dispersion of light.
questions.solution:
**Deviation of light:** The bending of a single ray (or single colour) of light from its original straight path when it passes through a prism or a slab, by an angle $\delta$.
$$\delta = i + e - A$$
It occurs even for **monochromatic** light.

**Dispersion of light:** The splitting of white light into its constituent colours because different colours are deviated by different angles. It requires **polychromatic** (white) light.

**Key differences:** Deviation is a change in direction of one ray; dispersion is a separation of colours, so $\text{dispersion} > \text{deviation}$ for white light. A red glass slab disperses (gives colour) but a plain glass slab of same shape only deviates.
questions.knowledgeNote: Deviation bends a single ray of light; dispersion splits white light into colours due to varying refractive index.
questions.answer: **Deviation of light:** the total angular deflection of a ray from its original direction after passing through an optical element (prism, slab, lens) — a **single-ray** effect, measured for one colour (usually yellow/mean light): δ = i + e − A for a prism. **Dispersion of light:** the **splitting of composite (white) light into its component colours** because n depends on wavelength — a **many-ray** effect measured by the angular spread between extreme colours (δ_v − δ_r) or by dispersive power. **Key differences:** (1) deviation is about one ray's bending; dispersion is about the *separation* of rays of different colours; (2) deviation occurs even for monochromatic light; dispersion requires polychromatic light and wavelength-dependent n; (3) deviation measures how *much* the prism bends light, dispersion measures how *unequally* it bends it. **Deep point:** a prism deviates *and* disperses simultaneously — deviation is the mean shift, dispersion the spread around it; an achromatic combination cancels the spread while keeping the shift.
